subject: Request: operational grace window for beta-grammar model (Lexicon Labs pilot)
messages:
From: Priya Rao <priya@lexlab.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@lexlab.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot go-live + ask: temporary SLA grace window for beta-grammar model

Ava —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Lexicon Labs is planning a small pilot of the new grammar-correction model (v1-beta-gram) starting 2027-06-21. Our product team expects an initial spike of ~8–12 qps during peak testing over the first two weeks while we tune prompts and filters.

We raised this because the model is still in preview: latency occasionally spikes (cold KV loads + longer decode paths) and we want to avoid triggering availability/latency penalties in the first 10 business days. Would Redwood consider an "operational grace window" (no SLA deductions / no automated throttling escalations) for 14 calendar days after pilot launch, conditional on agreed monitoring/rollforward criteria?

Attached is a short request with projected traffic, trial dates, and contact info. Happy to hop on a quick call if helpful.

Best,
Priya Rao
Head of Product, Lexicon Labs
[Attachment: lexicon_slo_request.pdf (PDF)]

From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Pilot go-live + ask: temporary SLA grace window for beta-grammar model

Team — forwarding Lexicon's request. They want a 14-day operational grace window for v1-beta-gram during their pilot (starts 6/21). Key asks: no SLA deductions / no automated throttling, conditional monitoring, and a signed amendment.

Can you please confirm feasibility and operational guardrails by EOD tomorrow? Specifically:
- Dev: what are the concrete risks to other tenants if we apply an exception (routing, burst capacity, fallback)?
- Product/Legal: what contract language and limits do we need (region, capacity, rollback criteria)?
- Ops: any quick mitigations we can enable (limited quota, dedicated pool, prefault KV loads)?

Attaching their request.

Thanks — Ava
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: lexicon_slo_request.pdf (PDF)]

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 09:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pilot go-live + ask: temporary SLA grace window for beta-grammar model

Ava / team — quick technical readout:

Summary: We can support a conditional 14-day grace window, but it must be paired with conservative runtime controls. Without limits, v1-beta-gram's cold KV behavior and longer decode loops increase tail latency and could push queuing on shared routing.

Proposed operational controls (recommended):
- Dedicated reserved tranche: add Lexicon to a small dedicated pool (1 GPU node) for the pilot window to contain tail latency impact.
- Strict QPS cap and circuit breaker: cap peak QPS to 15; circuit breaker triggers at p95 latency > 1200ms for >5min and falls back to a quantized v1-gram-q4 model.
- Prefetch/priming: preload KV caches for their seed prompts before live traffic (scheduled window each night).
- Telemetry hooks: create a per-route dashboard with latency, queue depth, dropped requests; add automated paging to oncall at two threshold bands.

Risks: dedicated pool consumes capacity that could otherwise absorb spikes from other customers; we'll need to schedule capacity ahead of 6/21. Also, the fallback path yields reduced answer quality—must be acceptable to Lexicon.

I'll open an INF ticket and provisioning request today (INF-5421). I can also provide a simplified rollback playbook for SRE to follow.

— Dev
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
[Attachment: operational-mitigation-checklist.xlsx (XLSX)]

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 14:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pilot go-live + ask: temporary SLA grace window for beta-grammar model

Ava / team — legal/product input:

We can accommodate a timeboxed operational grace window, but with the following constraints:
1) Exception limited to the US region and to Lexicon's account_id; no cross-account spillover.
2) Require a signed SLA amendment that explicitly documents the duration (14 calendar days), monitoring obligations, rollback criteria, and the fallback model behavior.
3) No blanket removal of penalties — we will suspend automated financial deductions tied to latency for the window, but other non-latency SLOs (data isolation/uptime) remain enforceable.
4) Dedicated pool recommendation aligns with dev; legal would prefer a clause stating Redwood may pause the pilot if cascading impact is detected.

Operational ask for Sales: provide the exact start/end dates and expected daily qps so we can scope the amendment and provisioning costs.

I've drafted a short amendment and attached it (slo-amendment-draft.docx). If Sales confirms, we should route for DocuSign and add a HubSpot note (HS-9321).

— Laura
Sr. Product Counsel, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: slo-amendment-draft.docx (DOCX)]

From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Rao <priya@lexlab.com>
Cc: procurement@lexlab.com, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 15:34:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Pilot go-live + ask: temporary SLA grace window for beta-grammar model

Priya —

Thanks for the note and for the attachment. We can offer a 14-calendar-day operational grace window starting on 2027-06-21 and ending on 2027-07-04 under the conditions below:

1) Dedicated pool: Lexicon will be placed into a one-node reserved pool for the pilot (US region). This isolates tail latency and contains risk.
2) QPS cap & fallback: Peak QPS capped at 15; automatic fallback to v1-gram-q4 if routed p95 latency > 1200ms for >5 consecutive minutes.
3) Monitoring & paging: We'll stand up a per-route dashboard (INF-5421) and configure two alert levels; SRE paging is part of level 2.
4) Contract amendment: Approval contingent on a signed amendment (DocuSign link will be sent). Within the amendment we will suspend automated financial latency deductions for the 14-day window only; other SLA terms (uptime, security) remain in effect.

I've attached the draft amendment and the operational checklist. Please confirm the start date (we used 2027-06-21) and expected peak qps/day so we can provision and generate the DocuSign envelope. Once signed we'll provision the dedicated tranche and run a pre-warm cycle on 2027-06-20.

If this sounds good, can procurement sign the amendment and we will kick off provisioning?

Best,
Ava Chen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachments: slo-amendment-draft.docx (DOCX), operational-mitigation-checklist.xlsx (XLSX)]
